# Connecting Energy, by Yorik Tisseau

> Connecting Energy is a free podcast and Substack by Yorik Tisseau about how the energy system fits together: generation, grid, demand and the people who build it. Yorik also advises energy developers on their commercial function through Ignis Leadership.

Yorik Tisseau has worked in renewables since 2013, at bp, RWE and Bouygues, on projects from early-stage development to financial close. He started as a plumber and boiler engineer and went on to lead offshore wind bids. Connecting Energy is his independent view of the energy transition across generation, grid and demand.

## Connecting Energy

- [Home](https://www.ignisleadership.com/): what the Connecting Energy podcast is, the first episodes (coming soon), how to be a guest, and the latest long reads from the Substack.

Free PDF with an email.
- [Route to Market for Energy Developers](https://www.ignisleadership.com/resources/route-to-market): CfD rounds, merchant, corporate PPAs and private wire, for onshore and offshore projects in the UK and Europe. Rounds are crowded. Winners pick their route early and arrive with the case built.
- [Procurement for Energy Developers](https://www.ignisleadership.com/resources/procurement): How developers fast-track supplier choice, contracts and the lender pack, onshore and offshore, with the team they have.

## Practical insights

- [RFP software or a bespoke agentic bid workflow?](https://www.ignisleadership.com/resources): a buyer guide comparing established proposal-response software with a governed workflow designed around complex bid work, including when the right answer is both.
- [Why do unclear tenders produce incomparable bids?](https://www.ignisleadership.com/insights/why-do-unclear-tenders-produce-incomparable-bids): how unclear requirements, interfaces and evaluation methods cause suppliers to answer different versions of the tender.
- [When do tender clarifications become a second specification?](https://www.ignisleadership.com/insights/when-do-tender-clarifications-become-a-second-specification): when clarification answers alter scope, risk or evidence, the log becomes part of the controlled commercial baseline.
- [Is commercial work too judgement-heavy for AI agents?](https://www.ignisleadership.com/insights/is-commercial-work-too-judgement-heavy-for-ai-agents): why the work surrounding commercial decisions suits governed agents precisely because the decisions must remain human.

Britain has backed a rise in electricity to 35% of final energy use by 2035. The quickest way to get there is to use the wires we already have, better.

- [Who powers the next data centre?](https://www.ignisleadership.com/insights/who-powers-the-next-data-centre): Signal Issue 3 on data centres, grid capacity and the commercial openings for energy developers.
- [First come, first served is over. What the new grid offers mean for developers](https://www.ignisleadership.com/insights/what-gate-2-is-really-about): for years, grid connections ran on first come, first served: apply early and you kept your place in the queue, ready or not.
- [AO10: why proof, not price, decides France's round](https://www.ignisleadership.com/insights/ao10-france-has-put-a-price-on-proof): AO10 turns the credibility of a French offshore wind bid into points, and those points translate almost one for one into euros per MWh for developers.

## Key concepts used on this site

- Governed human-AI system: a commercial operating model that combines the team's process, evidence and judgement with bounded agent tasks, named decision rights and human approval.
- Commercial memory: the usable record of what an organisation believed, why it believed it, what changed and who has authority to make the next commitment.
- Human accountability: agents prepare and coordinate while named people retain authority to direct, challenge, decide and approve.
- Modular adoption: start with one useful pilot, prove it under real conditions, then extend the system one capability at a time.

## Questions this site answers

### What can AI agents safely do in bids and tenders?

Agents can extract, reconcile, draft, check and coordinate bounded work using approved evidence and controls. People retain authority for strategy, relationships, price, risk, evaluation and every material commitment.

### How do you govern AI in bids and tenders?

Give agents approved evidence, bounded tasks and explicit controls. Keep named people responsible for strategy, evaluation, price, risk and final approval. Preserve the evidence and decision trail so outputs can be challenged and verified.

### Where should a bid or tender team start with agentic AI?

Start with one pressure point in live work. Audit the process, evidence, decisions and controls; prove one bounded capability; measure what changes; then scale only what the evidence supports.
